title_en: Stories of Modern China (20/20): The Reunion Dinner
note_en: 得 after a verb introduces how well or to what degree something was done: 把老家守得好好的 "kept the old home in good shape," literally "looked after it so that it is good and fine." Where English uses an adverb ("looked after it well"), Chinese puts the verb first and the description of the result after 得; doubling the adjective (好好的) makes it warmer and more vivid.
